newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile cobalt sales to remain suspended.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile cobalt sales to remain suspended.

text.p: Sales of U.S. government cobalt will remain suspended until at least mid-June until issues stemming from a legal battle between the agency and trader Minor Metals Inc is resolved.

In a written ruling released late Tuesday, Judge Tidwell of the Court of Federal Claims in Washington, D.C., dismissed Minor Metals' first count complaint that the U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center had no right to prohibit "all or none" bids when it sold cobalt.
"The first count of the plaintiff's complaint is dismissed," Tidwell said in his ruling.
Minor Metals, on a second count, had also complained Stockpile was illegally using a domestic preference provision to sell cobalt in the sealed bid sale for 1 million pounds of metal in March.
This preference allows a company which would dispose of the cobalt domestically to match a bid from a company which would export the metal awarded in a sealed bid sale.
"The court finds defendant (Stockpile) does have the authority to utilize a domestic preference provision," Judge Tidwell said in his conclusion.
But Tidwell added it was "procedurally improper" to combine elements of a formally advertised solicitation (sealed bid) with that of a competitive negotiation solicitation.

Due to the "procedurally improper soliciation", Tidwell granted Minor Metals a preliminary injunction that prevents Stockpile from going ahead with one million-lb March DLA Cobalt 005 soliciation "until this matter is finally concluded".
"This court orders the parties to confer and to report back to the court as to how they wish to proceed by June 13, 1997," Tidwell said in the ruling.
Lawyers and executives for Minor Metals were not immediately available for comment on the judge's ruling.
Stockpile's attorney Essie Schloss said the preliminary injunction would make no difference and formalised what was already in effect.

Schloss said Stockpile had agreed voluntarily at the outset to suspend all cobalt sales until the Court of Federal Claims case and another separate case, also involving a complaint by Minor Metals in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, were resolved.

Earlier this month, Judge Ellis of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia dismissed a Minor Metals complaint and scrapped a temporary restraining order that had been slapped on February's Stockpile negotiated sale of cobalt.
Although Tuesday's ruling and preliminary injunction refers to March's sealed bid, Stockpile will not go ahead with any negotiated bid sales in the meantime, Schloss said.
"We are not going to do anything until the matter is resolved," Schloss said.
Dealers have said cobalt prices have been firmer partly due to Stockpile suspending sales of some 1 million pounds each in March, April and May.

Tidwell said although it was in the public interest to continue with the sale, "it is not in the public interest to allow a fundamentally flawed government soliciation to proceed when there are known defects which can be cured."
